title: Joash and Jehoiada
lead: Joash, the only survivor of Athaliah's purge, was hidden in the Temple and crowned at seven by the priest Jehoiada. He reigned forty years (about 835–796 BC), repaired the Temple, and was murdered by his own servants; Chronicles adds that after Jehoiada died he turned to idols and had Jehoiada's son Zechariah stoned.

sections.b: For six years one hidden boy was all that remained of David's line (2 Kings 11:1–3; 2 Chronicles 22:10–12). Jehoiada's coup restored the dynasty and renewed the covenant (2 Kings 11:4–20; 2 Chronicles 23). Kings and Chronicles both tell of the Temple repair and the money chest (2 Kings 12:4–16; 2 Chronicles 24:4–14), and both of his murder (2 Kings 12:20–21; 2 Chronicles 24:25–26). Only Chronicles divides his reign into faithful years under Jehoiada and an apostasy afterward (2 Chronicles 24:2, 17–22).
